name: Third-person 3D character and camera
oneLiner: A low-poly adventurer on a small 3D island seen from a smooth follow camera: camera-relative movement (keys or touch stick), idle / walk / run animated from the distance travelled so feet never slide, models auto-scaled by bounding box with feet on the ground in every pose, a facing rule (yaw = atan2(v.x, v.z) + facingOffset) checked against the model's real forward vector, a camera that pulls in when a prop blocks the view, pickups, NPCs that turn to face the hero, world-to-screen anchors and a 2D overlay layer for addons.
fits: third-person action or RPG prototypes (before combat is added)
walking-sim and story games with NPCs to talk to
a 3D hub area inside a larger game
notFor: 2D side or top-down games (use the 2D movement elements)
physics platformers with jumps and ledges (no jumping or slopes in this element)

needs: three.js 0.149.0 classic build loaded as window.THREE before the module
a canvas for WebGL and (optional) a 2D canvas on top for HUD and addons
a fixed 60 Hz step that passes camera-relative input {x, y, run}
the world content: prop list (kind, x, z, rot, scale), pickups, NPCs
provides: events: pickup {id, kind, value, x, z}; the starter adds onTalk, onPhase, onEnd, onStep
actors() with x, z, yaw, speed, target; anchor(id) -> screen px of head top, feet and centre (world -> screen)
project(x, y, z) -> screen px; the 2D overlay layers world | hud | overlay
state(): {t, actors:[{id, x, z, yaw, moveDir, forward, target, facesMove, facesTarget, feetY, pose}]} for checks
autopilot(goal) -> camera-relative input along an A* path around props

assets: module/third-person-3d.js (global GameDNA_ThirdPerson3D; needs three.js 0.149.0 as window.THREE, copied as three.min.js next to the page). All models, props and textures are procedural (primitives, code-drawn canvas textures). No external files besides three.min.js.
